whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim, and nothing else. It says who wrote the compliance-path files below and on which issue. It asserts nothing about whether they are correct, and it carries no `reviews[]` entry.
doesNotClaimR2: There is no `reviews[]` entry here and there will not be one from me. R2 wants a named reviewer who is not the author, and I am the author of every path above. This migration touches the permission layer (grants DML on directus_* tables whose activity/revision rows can snapshot application row content), so under the team rule it goes to the CTO, and there is no independent security reviewer on this team (board declined the seat on cost) -- a CTO self-review is a recorded degradation, not independent review. The commit carrying these three compliance-path files WILL report an R2 violation until that review records its verdict, and that violation is the honest state. Writing a `reviews[]` entry naming myself would turn a control into a rubber stamp.
scopeOfTheClaim: R1 only: authorship of the listed paths on AFC-783. It is not clearance of the retention gate (plan 0.10.5), which only the CEO can clear, and it does not record that the staging re-try is safe -- the live Directus boot as directus_app with /server/health and an API round-trip is an operator checklist item (runbook section 8.5), proven on staging, not in this commit.
whatTheChangeActuallyDoes: AFC-783 follow-up to AFC-749: the Directus 11 runtime grant matrix. Migration 0042 grants directus_app uniform SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on every migrator-owned directus_* table (prefix loop, so minor-version additions are covered at the next apply), USAGE+SELECT on directus_* sequences, revokes PUBLIC, and refuses with restrict_violation while any directus_* table or sequence is foreign-owned (naming the operator transfer step). No new role (Directus holds a single DB_USER), no per-table carve-outs, no TRUNCATE, no DDL, no default privileges, no ownership change, no application-table grant. The down script revokes best-effort and drops no control. Suite 42 (19 assertions) covers the matrix on migrator-owned probes, the TRUNCATE/PUBLIC denials, the fail-closed refusal naming the foreign object, the intact application-table ceiling (incidents stays SELECT-only), and the rollback/re-apply cycle.
verificationRecorded: Full DB suite green locally (PGlite): 52 suites, 1913 assertions, 0 failing, including the new 42_directus_runtime_matrix.sql. Static gates green: migration-privilege (+self-test), retention-literal, rollback-control, awareness-write-context, adr-uniqueness, credential-surface-scan self-test. Bootstrap owns-nothing/CREATE-less assertions proven both directions on PGlite (clean apply passes; an owned table and a CREATE grant each refuse with the named message, then revoke converges). Real-Postgres (CI PG16) and live Directus boot proof are operator/CI steps, not claimed here.
